# BlockingRuns — blocking runs and the largest survivor gap

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [Gaps between survivors and between primes](../../GRAPH.md#gaps-between-survivors-and-between-primes)

A setting of the wheels (one blocked position per wheel) is a shift of the ordinary sieve, by the Chinese Remainder Theorem; so a run of consecutive numbers can be blocked by some setting exactly when some gap between consecutive survivors is at least one longer. The longest blocked run is one less than the largest survivor gap (Jacobsthal's function of the cycle length). With JacobsthalQuadratic, such runs are at most a constant times the square of the number of wheels. Checked numerically beforehand for the wheels below 14 over every setting.

## Claims

<a id="blocked_run_is_shift"></a>
### `blocked_run_is_shift`

A run blocked by any setting of the wheels reappears, shifted, as a run of numbers each divisible by some wheel.

```lean
/-- **Every setting of the wheels is a shift of the ordinary sieve.** For the
wheels below `limit`, a setting `b` (one blocked position per wheel), and a
run of `L` numbers from `s` each landing on its blocked position on some
wheel: there is a starting point `s'` (at least 1) from which `L` consecutive
numbers are each divisible by some wheel. -/
def blocked_run_is_shift : Prop :=
  ∀ (limit s L : Nat) (b : ∀ q : active_primes limit, ZMod (q : Nat)),
    (∀ i < L, ∃ q : active_primes limit, ((s + i : Nat) : ZMod (q : Nat)) = b q) →
    ∃ s', 1 ≤ s' ∧ ∀ i < L, ∃ q ∈ active_primes limit, q ∣ s' + i
```

**Rests on:** [`CRT.crt_map_bijective`](CRT.md#crt_map_bijective)

**Proof:** `RNS.BlockingRuns.blocked_run_is_shift_step` in [`RNSSolutions/BlockingRuns.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/BlockingRuns.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="longest_blocked_run_eq_max_gap_sub_one"></a>
### `longest_blocked_run_eq_max_gap_sub_one`

Some setting blocks a run of a given length exactly when some gap between consecutive survivors is at least one longer.

```lean
/-- **The longest blocked run is one less than the largest survivor gap.** For
the wheels below `limit` and a length `L`: some setting of the wheels blocks
a run of `L` consecutive numbers exactly when there are two consecutive
survivors `a < c` (no survivor strictly between) with `c - a` at least
`L + 1`. -/
def longest_blocked_run_eq_max_gap_sub_one : Prop :=
  ∀ (limit L : Nat),
    (∃ (b : ∀ q : active_primes limit, ZMod (q : Nat)) (s : Nat),
        ∀ i < L, ∃ q : active_primes limit, ((s + i : Nat) : ZMod (q : Nat)) = b q) ↔
    (∃ a c : Nat, (∀ q ∈ active_primes limit, ¬ q ∣ a) ∧ (∀ q ∈ active_primes limit, ¬ q ∣ c) ∧
        a < c ∧ (∀ m, a < m → m < c → ∃ q ∈ active_primes limit, q ∣ m) ∧ L + 1 ≤ c - a)
```

**Rests on:** [`BlockingRuns.blocked_run_is_shift`](BlockingRuns.md#blocked_run_is_shift)

**Proof:** `RNS.BlockingRuns.longest_blocked_run_eq_max_gap_sub_one_step` in [`RNSSolutions/BlockingRuns.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/BlockingRuns.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)
